title: Request user authorization
content_data:
Use this endpoint to open a browser-based authorization page where the user signs in to TikTok for Business and approves your request. After the user grants approval, the server redirects the browser to your registered `redirect_uri` with an authorization code. > **Note**
> • For security reasons, the user might be required to complete email verification to authorize the request. If you need to bypass this verification step for a trusted client and `redirect_uri`, contact your TikTok representative. >
> • Do not hardcode the authorization URL. Always dynamically retrieve it from the `authorization_endpoint` field in [/open_mcp/{server}/oauth/.well-known/openid-configuration/](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs/get-authorization-server-metadata/v1.3). # Request **Endpoint** https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/mcp-tt4b-authorize/ **Method** GET **Query parameters** ```xtable |Field{28%}|Data Type{18%}|Description{54%}| |---|---|---| |response_type {Required}|string|The requested response type.

Enum value:
  • `code`: You will receive an authorization code to exchange for a token.
| |resource {Required}|string|The specific TikTok for Business MCP server URL.

Enum values:
  • `https://business-api.tiktok.com/open_mcp/tt-ads-mcp-flat`
  • `https://business-api.tiktok.com/open_mcp/tt-ads-mcp-layer`

To learn more about how these server URLs differ, see [Choose your server URL](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs/how-to-connect-a-custom-agent-to-tiktok-for-business-mcp-server/v1.3#anchor-3).| |client_id {Required}|string|The registered client ID.

Ensure this ID exists and is valid.

To obtain the client ID, use [/open_mcp/{server}/oauth/register/](https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/docs/register-a-client-application/v1.3).| |redirect_uri {Required}|string|The redirect URI for this specific authorization request.

Ensure it exactly matches one of the redirect URIs you registered for the client application.| |scope {Required}|string|The requested permission scope.

Enum value:
  • `mcp:tt4b`: the necessary permissions to access TikTok for Business MCP server features.
| |state|string|A random string generated by your client application.

The server will echo this exact value back to your `redirect_uri` upon redirection. You need to verify that the returned value matches the one you originally sent.

You are highly recommended to include this to prevent Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks and for request tracking.| |code_challenge {Required}|string|The PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) code challenge string, a hashed version of a random secret string (the `code_verifier`) generated by your client application.

This is part of the PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) security flow, which prevents hackers from intercepting your authorization code by creating a dynamic, one-time secret for every login.

To create the string, follow these steps:
  1. Generate a `code_verifier` (a random, secure string between 43 and 128 characters).
  2. Create the `code_challenge` by hashing your `code_verifier` using SHA-256 and Base64-URL encoding the result.
  3. Send this challenge now. Later, when exchanging your authorization code for an access token, you will send the original `code_verifier`. The server will compare them to prove that the application exchanging the code is the exact same app that requested it.
| |code_challenge_method {Required}|string|The hashing algorithm used to create your `code_challenge` from your `code_verifier`.

Enum value:
  • `S256`: To securely hash your `code_verifier` using the SHA-256 algorithm before sending it.
| ``` ## Example > **Note**
> The example below uses `https://business-api.tiktok.com/open_mcp/tt-ads-mcp-layer` as the `{{resource}}` value. You can replace this with your chosen server value. ```xcodeblock (code curl http) https://business-api.tiktok.com/portal/mcp-tt4b-authorize?response_type=code&resource=https://business-api.tiktok.com/open_mcp/tt-ads-mcp-layer&client_id={{client_id}}&redirect_uri={{redirect_uri}}&scope=mcp:tt4b&code_challenge={{code_challenge}}&code_challenge_method=S256 (/code) ``` # Response On approval, the authorization server redirects the browser to the specified `redirect_uri` with the following query parameters. ```xtable |Field{28%}|Data Type{18%}|Description{54%}| |---|---|---| | code | string | The authorization code granted to you after user approval. | | state | string | Returned only when `state` is included in the request.
The state value echoed back from your initial request. | ``` ## Example ```xcodeblock (code curl http) https://example.com/oauth/callback?code={{code}}&state={{state}} (/code) ``` ## Error response Authorization failures are rendered on the authorization page in the user's browser rather than returned as JSON.
